en.title: Cronos Halted After $75M Exploit; Sberbank Backs Crypto Loans
en.body:
A $75 million exploit forced Crypto.com's Cronos blockchain to halt entirely on August 31, while institutional momentum continued with Sberbank accepting Ethereum and Tether as loan collateral and Strategy resuming Bitcoin purchases after a two-month pause.

The Tectonic exploit on Cronos blockchain represents one of the larger DeFi attacks this year. Hackers managed to move approximately $6 million to Ethereum before validators froze the chain, leaving remaining funds stranded on a network that stopped producing blocks. The incident underscores persistent smart contract vulnerabilities even on established Layer-1 networks and raises questions about response protocols for major exchange-operated chains.

In Russia, Sberbank announced plans to accept ETH and USDT as collateral for crypto-backed loans. The Bank of Russia recently included both assets in a draft list of cryptocurrencies approved for trading on Russian exchanges, signaling potential normalization of digital asset use in traditional banking products. The development comes as multiple Russian financial institutions explore crypto integration despite ongoing regulatory complexities.

Strategy, the Michael Saylor-led Bitcoin treasury company, returned to acquisition markets after roughly two months without purchases. The firm added $370 million worth of Bitcoin during the week ending August 31, its first weekly buy in approximately eight weeks. The resumption of buying activity coincides with Bitcoin approaching its August monthly close below key resistance levels, with markets now pricing increased probability of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in September.

On the protocol level, Hyperliquid and Pump.fun together accounted for nearly 90 percent of a record $638 million in token buybacks across the crypto market in 2026. The concentration suggests a few high-volume platforms are increasingly returning revenue directly to token holders, a trend that could pressure competing protocols to adopt similar shareholder-friendly mechanisms.

Bitcoin faced headwinds as the monthly close approached, with price action staying below significant technical resistance. Traders cited the Fed rate-hike pivot as a factor pressuring risk assets broadly. The combination of institutional accumulation, persistent security concerns, and shifting monetary policy expectations paints a complex near-term outlook for digital asset markets.
